q: What do we know about feat-sfc-cpi-lag6 in the spend-forecasting project?
a: A six-month lag of year-on-year CPI added to sfc-lgbm-v2 in August 2025 (exp-204). It improves 1-month MAPE by 0.1pp, but 3-month MAPE by 0.4pp and 6-month MAPE by 0.6pp.

q: What came of exp-206 in the spend-forecasting project?
a: exp-206 tested Prophet on sfc-bt-2024: 6.9% 1-month MAPE, worse than sfc-lgbm-v2 at 5.1%, and about 40 times slower to fit. dec-sfc-drop-prophet dropped it.

q: What does sfc-hier-v3 depend on in the spend-forecasting project?
a: Per-segment LightGBM base forecasts built on feat-sfc-lags-v1, feat-sfc-season-v2, feat-sfc-cpi-lag6 and feat-sfc-active-accounts, reconciled with MinT across segments and the total. The source table is ds-sfc-segment-monthly.

q: What is the current segment spend forecast model in the spend-forecasting project?
a: sfc-hier-v3, adopted 10 Feb 2026 in place of sfc-lgbm-v2. It is refit on the first working day of each month (dec-sfc-monthly-refit).

q: What total-level MAPE does sfc-hier-v3 reach on sfc-oot-2025h2 in the spend-forecasting project?
a: 2.3% total-level MAPE and 4.9% segment-level MAPE on sfc-oot-2025h2 (Jul-Dec 2025), against 2.9% and 5.1% for sfc-lgbm-v2.

q: Why was the spend-forecasting Q4 segment forecast bias fixed?
a: sfc-lgbm-v2 under-forecast November and December by 3.1% on sfc-oot-2025h2, because the segments were forecast independently and did not add up to the total. MinT reconciliation in exp-207 brought the Q4 bias to -0.4%.
